questions.question: A quantity which requires magnitude and direction to be specified is
questions.explanation: A vector quantity requires both magnitude and direction. Displacement is a vector, while temperature, distance, and mass are scalars.

questions.question: I. Electrical potential, II. Torque, III. Kinetic Energy, IV. Momentum. Which of the quantities listed are vectors?
questions.explanation: Torque and momentum are vectors. Electrical potential and kinetic energy are scalars. Therefore, II and IV are vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Altitude is a scalar (height above a reference level). Acceleration, displacement, and weight are vectors.

questions.question: The pair of physical quantities that are scalar only are
questions.explanation: Volume and area are both scalars. Moment and momentum are vectors. Displacement and impulse are vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a set of vectors?
questions.explanation: Acceleration, velocity, and moment (torque) are all vectors. Mass, density, volume are scalars; weight is a vector but mixed with scalars in other options.

questions.question: Which of the following quantities are scalars? i. Electrical potential ii. Torque iii. Momentum iv. Kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Electrical potential and kinetic energy are scalars. Torque and momentum are vectors. So i and iv only.

questions.question: Each of the following physical quantities is classified as a vector or a scalar quantity. Which of the classifications is correct?
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density is a vector. Electric potential is scalar, momentum is vector, gravitational field intensity is vector.

questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities is NOT a vector?
questions.explanation: Work is a scalar quantity. Velocity, force, and electric field intensity are vectors.

questions.question: An example of a scalar quantity is
questions.explanation: Electric charge is a scalar. Velocity, weight, and acceleration due to gravity are vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar. Tension, weight, and impulse are vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance is scalar. Momentum, acceleration, and displacement are vectors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Altitude is a scalar. Force, weight, and displacement are vectors.

questions.question: The pair of physical quantities consisting of vectors only are
questions.explanation: Displacement and torque are both vectors. Momentum is vector but power scalar; velocity vector, distance scalar; acceleration vector, speed scalar.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Temperature gradient is a vector (it has direction of maximum increase of temperature). Mass, work, and time are scalars.

questions.question: I. A scalar quantity has only magnitude. II. A scalar quantity has both magnitude and direction. III. A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. IV. A vector quantity has only magnitude. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. A scalar has only magnitude; a vector has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector?
questions.explanation: Electric field is a vector. Electric charge, potential difference, and capacitance are scalars.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities comprises vectors?
questions.explanation: Friction (a force) and momentum are vectors. Capacitance, inductance, ratios, energy, and power are scalars.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities is made up of vectors?
questions.explanation: Displacement and acceleration are both vectors. Speed, mass, length are scalars; force and momentum are vectors but mixed with scalars.

questions.question: A vector quantity can only be completely described when ______ and ______ are mentioned.
questions.explanation: A vector is completely specified by its magnitude and direction.

questions.question: Two forces whose resultant is 100N are at right angles to each other. If one of them makes an angle of 30° with the resultant, determine its magnitude.
questions.explanation: For two perpendicular forces, the angle α between one force F₁ and the resultant R satisfies cos α = F₁/R. Thus F₁ = R cos 30° = 100 × 0.866 = 86.6 N.

questions.question: The magnitude of the resultant of two mutually perpendicular forces, F₁ and F₂ is 13N. If the magnitude of F₁ is 5N, what is the magnitude of F₂?
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras: R² = F₁² + F₂². 13² = 5² + F₂² ⇒ 169 = 25 + F₂² ⇒ F₂² = 144 ⇒ F₂ = 12 N.

questions.question: Two forces of magnitudes 7N and 3N act at right angles to each other. The angle θ between the resultant and the 7N force is given by
questions.explanation: For perpendicular forces, tan θ = (opposite force)/(adjacent force) = 3/7, where θ is the angle between the resultant and the 7 N force.

questions.question: The resultant of two forces is 50N. If the forces are perpendicular to each other and one of them makes an angle of 30° with the resultant, find its magnitude.
questions.explanation: As in a similar case, F = R cos 30° = 50 × 0.866 = 43.3 N.

questions.question: Two forces 3N and 4N act on a body in directions due north and due east respectively. Calculate their equilibrant.
questions.explanation: Resultant = √(3² + 4²) = 5 N. The angle with east is tan⁻¹(3/4) = 37°, so the resultant is 5 N at 37° north of east. The equilibrant is opposite, but the option matching the resultant direction is C.

questions.question: The resultant of two forces 12N and 5N is 13N. What is the angle between the two forces?
questions.explanation: R² = F₁² + F₂² + 2F₁F₂ cos θ. 13² = 12² + 5² + 2(12)(5) cos θ ⇒ 169 = 144 + 25 + 120 cos θ ⇒ 0 = 120 cos θ ⇒ cos θ = 0 ⇒ θ = 90°.

questions.question: Two forces each of 10N act on a body, one towards the north and the other towards the east. The magnitude and the direction of the resultant force are
questions.explanation: Perpendicular forces: R = √(10² + 10²) = 10√2 N. The resultant points north-east, i.e., 45° east of north.

questions.question: Two forces, whose resultant is 100N, are perpendicular to each other. If one of them makes an angle of 60° with the resultant, calculate the magnitude.
A boat travels due east at a speed of 40ms⁻¹ across a river flowing due south at 30ms⁻¹. What is the resultant speed of the boat?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular velocities: R = √(40² + 30²) = √(1600 + 900) = √2500 = 50.0 m/s.

questions.question: A man walks 8km north and then 5km in a direction 60° east of north. Find the distance from his starting point.
questions.explanation: First displacement: (0,8). Second: 5 km at 60° east of north gives east = 5 sin60 = 4.33, north = 5 cos60 = 2.5. Total north = 10.5, east = 4.33. Distance = √(10.5² + 4.33²) = √(110.25 + 18.75) = √129 ≈ 11.36 km.

questions.question: A man walks 1km due east and then 1km due north. His displacement is
questions.explanation: Displacement = √(1² + 1²) = √2 km. The direction is 45° east of north (north-east).

questions.question: A lorry travels 10km northwards, 4km eastwards, 6km southwards, 4km westwards to arrive at a point T. What is the total displacement?
questions.explanation: Net north-south = 10 − 6 = 4 km north. Net east-west = 4 − 4 = 0. So displacement is 4 km north.

questions.question: An aircraft attempts to fly due north at 100kmh⁻¹. If the wind blows against it from east to west at 60kmh⁻¹, its resultant velocity is
questions.explanation: Velocity = north 100 + west 60. Magnitude = √(100² + 60²) = √13600 ≈ 116.6 ≈ 117 km/h. Angle west of north = tan⁻¹(60/100) ≈ 31°. So N31°W.

questions.question: An aircraft travelled from Calabar to Kano as follows: it flew first to Ilorin covering a distance of 300km, 30° west of North, and then flew 400km, 60° East of North to Kano. What is the resultant displacement?
questions.explanation: First leg: north = 300 cos30 = 259.8, west = 300 sin30 = 150. Second leg: north = 400 cos60 = 200, east = 400 sin60 = 346.4. Net north = 459.8, net east = 196.4. Resultant = √(459.8² + 196.4²) ≈ 500 km.

questions.question: A motorcyclist, passing a road junction, moves due west for 8s at a uniform speed of 5ms⁻¹. He then moves due north for another 6s with the same speed. At the end of the 6s his displacement from the road junction is 50m in the direction of
questions.explanation: West displacement = 5×8 = 40 m. North displacement = 5×6 = 30 m. Resultant = √(40² + 30²) = 50 m. Angle west of north = tan⁻¹(40/30) = 53.13° ≈ 53°W. So N53°W.

questions.question: A ball is moving at 18ms⁻¹ in a direction inclined at 60° to the horizontal. The horizontal component of its velocity is
questions.explanation: Horizontal component = v cos θ = 18 cos 60° = 18 × 0.5 = 9 m/s.

questions.question: A body of weight W N rests on a smooth plane inclined at an angle θ° to the horizontal. What is the resolved part of the weight in Newtons along the plane?
questions.explanation: The component of weight along the inclined plane is W sin θ. The perpendicular component is W cos θ.

questions.question: One of the conditions necessary for an object to be in equilibrium when acted upon by a number of parallel forces is that the vector sum of the forces is
questions.explanation: For equilibrium under parallel forces, the algebraic sum of the forces (vector sum) must be zero.

questions.question: What happens when three coplanar non-parallel forces are in equilibrium?
options: Their lines of action are parallel.
They are represented in magnitude only.
They are represented in direction only.
Their lines of action meet at a point.
questions.explanation: For three coplanar non-parallel forces to be in equilibrium, their lines of action must be concurrent (meet at a point).

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct about an object in equilibrium under parallel forces? i. The total clockwise moments of the forces about any point equals the total anti-clockwise moments about the same point. ii. The total forces in one direction equals the total forces in the opposite direction. iii. The resolved components along the x-axis equals the resolved components along the y-axis.
questions.explanation: For equilibrium: sum of forces in one direction equals sum in opposite (ii), and sum of clockwise moments equals sum of anticlockwise moments (i). Statement iii is incorrect.

questions.question: A particle of mass M which is at rest splits up into two. If the mass and velocity of one of the particles are m and v respectively, calculate the velocity of the second particle.
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: 0 = m v + (M−m) v₂ ⇒ v₂ = − m v / (M−m). Magnitude = mv/(M−m).

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.15kg is kicked against a rigid vertical wall with a horizontal velocity of 50ms⁻¹. If it rebounds with a horizontal velocity of 30ms⁻¹, calculate the impulse of the ball on the ball.
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v_f − v_i) = 0.15(−30 − 50) = 0.15(−80) = −12 Ns. Magnitude = 12.0 Ns.

questions.question: A body of mass 100g moving with a velocity of 10.0ms⁻¹ collides with a wall. If after collision, it moves with a velocity of 2.0ms⁻¹ in the opposite direction, calculate the change in momentum.
questions.explanation: Mass = 0.1 kg. Change = m(v_f − v_i) = 0.1(−2 − 10) = 0.1(−12) = −1.2 Ns. Magnitude = 1.2 Ns.

questions.question: A stone, Q is thrown with velocity U at an angle of 75° to the horizontal. Another stone R is thrown with the same velocity U but with an angle of 15° to the horizontal. The ranges covered by the stones will be
options: The same for Q and R
Greater for the heavier of the two stones
questions.explanation: For projectile motion, range depends on sin 2θ. Since 2(75°) = 150° and 2(15°) = 30°, and sin 150° = sin 30°, the ranges are equal.

questions.question: An object is projected with a velocity of 80ms⁻¹ at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. The maximum height reached is
A 5kg block is released from rest on a smooth plane inclined at an angle of 30° to the horizontal. What is the acceleration down the plane? [g = 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation: On a smooth incline, a = g sin θ = 10 × sin 30° = 10 × 0.5 = 5.0 m/s².

questions.question: The force of attraction between two point masses is 10⁻⁴N when the distance between them is 0.18m. If the distance is reduced to 0.06m, calculate the force.
questions.explanation: Force ∝ 1/r². Distance reduced by factor 3 (0.18/0.06 = 3). So force increases by 3² = 9. New force = 9 × 10⁻⁴ N.

questions.question: A rocket burns fuel at the rate of 10kgs⁻¹ and ejects it with a velocity of 5 × 10³ms⁻¹. The thrust exerted by the gas on the rocket is
questions.explanation: Thrust = velocity × rate of mass ejection = (5 × 10³) × 10 = 5 × 10⁴ N.

questions.question: The force with which an object is attracted to the earth is called its
questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force of attraction on an object.

questions.question: A vector of magnitude 10 units makes an angle of 60° with the positive x-axis. What is its y-component?
questions.explanation: y-component = magnitude × sin θ = 10 × sin 60° = 10 × 0.866 = 8.66.

questions.question: A particle starts from rest and moves with a constant acceleration of 0.5ms⁻². The distance covered by the particle in 10s is
questions.explanation: Distance s = ut + ½at². u = 0, a = 0.5, t = 10. s = ½ × 0.5 × 100 = 25.0 m.
